nodes.name: Player car handling
nodes.purpose: Per-frame steering input, speed-scaled steering lock, lateral slide build-up and recovery, cornering scrub and surface grip for the human-driven stock car

nodes.name: Engine, gearbox and draft
nodes.purpose: Gear bands that map speed to engine rpm, manual and automatic shifting, the per-frame drive force with off-band penalties, coasting loss and the slipstream speed bonus behind another car

nodes.name: Car and wall collision
nodes.purpose: Car-to-car contact with speed exchange, side impulses and the crash threshold, plus wall contact with scrape loss, rebound impulse and spark effects

nodes.name: Race control
nodes.purpose: Lap counting at the start-finish line, fuel use, running order, finishing penalties, caution periods and the scripted crashes that bring out the yellow flag

nodes.name: Opponent field driver
nodes.purpose: Computer cars that decide when a pass is possible, pick an avoidance point beside slower cars, and match speed when boxed in

cards.name: Digital steering ramp
cards.summary: With a digital pad the wheel angle grows by an accelerating step each frame and returns to center when released
cards.behavior: While a direction is held, the per-frame steering step starts at 4 and grows by 3 each frame up to 12. The wheel angle gains 4 plus the step each frame and stops at the current steering lock. The opposite step resets to zero, so a quick reversal starts slowly again. With no direction held, the angle returns toward center by 8 per frame and stops at zero. An analog stick instead sets the angle directly as stick deflection times the lock divided by 112. The heading input applied to the car is a quarter of the wheel angle. A quarter value of one in either direction counts as zero, which gives a small dead zone.

constants.name: firstStep
constants.unit: steering angle units per frame, rate unverified

constants.name: stepGrowth
constants.unit: steering angle units per frame per frame, rate unverified

constants.name: maxStep
constants.unit: steering angle units per frame, hexadecimal, rate unverified

constants.name: centerReturn
constants.unit: steering angle units per frame, rate unverified

constants.name: wheelToHeading
constants.unit: divisor from wheel angle to heading input, static

cards.name: Speed-scaled steering lock
cards.summary: Above a threshold speed the steering lock shrinks along a slope set by the car setup and its grip
cards.behavior: The base steering lock comes from the handling setup and is multiplied by 4. Two optional buttons scale it to three quarters or four thirds. Above speed 200, the lock is scaled by 1000 minus the speed over 200 times a slope divided by a grip divisor, in thousandths. The slope blends between two setup values by the steering setting, measured from 50 over a range of 50. The grip divisor is 3000 plus an orientation term weighted by 200, plus front grip times 35 and rear grip times 5. Higher grip therefore keeps more lock at speed. The lock never falls below 8.

constants.name: falloffStartSpeed
constants.unit: speed units, 16.16 fixed point integer part, scale unverified

cards.name: Lateral slide build-up
cards.summary: Steering at speed builds a sideways slide value that rear grip bleeds off, faster when counter-steering
cards.behavior: Below speed 100 the slide value is cleared and nothing happens. Above it, each frame adds two fifths of the steering angle times speed, weighted by half of throttle plus one, plus a fixed bias toward the steer side. That step is capped at the rear grip recovery plus 500. Rear grip times 100, minus 500, is then removed from the slide each frame toward zero. Steering against the slide doubles that recovery. The yaw force returned is the slide value times 16, clamped once its magnitude passes 1000 bands. Some slide bands set a slide feedback flag when the steering step exceeds the recovery.

constants.name: minSlideSpeed
constants.unit: speed units, 16.16 fixed point integer part, scale unverified

constants.name: steerShareNumerator
constants.unit: fraction numerator of steering angle, static

constants.name: steerShareDenominator
constants.unit: fraction denominator of steering angle, static

constants.name: recoveryOffset
constants.unit: slide units per frame, rate unverified

cards.name: Cornering scrub and speed loss
cards.summary: Cornering force grows with speed squared and tighter turns, and force past the tire hold scrubs speed and pushes the car outward
cards.behavior: Each frame, a cornering force equals speed squared times a car factor, divided by a term that shrinks as the turn input grows: 14 minus the turn, times 1000, plus 14000. The force doubles when it opposes the current slide. It joins the slide value together with an orientation term. A fixed decay pulls the slide toward zero, twice as hard when the car goes straight. Each of the four tires holds 2000 units of the slide. The excess, divided by 256 and then by 16, comes off forward speed, so overdriving a corner costs speed. The excess divided by 200 also pushes the car along its lateral axis.

constants.name: turnTermScale
constants.unit: divisor scale per turn step, static

constants.name: scrubDivisor
constants.unit: divisor on excess slide, then divided by 16, per frame, rate unverified

constants.name: lateralPushDivisor
constants.unit: divisor on excess slide, per frame, rate unverified

cards.name: Off-track surface grip
cards.summary: Each wheel reads a grip value from its surface code, and rough surfaces bleed wheel velocity and throw up debris
cards.behavior: A wheel on normal track returns a grip of one half. On surface code 2 the front wheels return one third and the rear wheels one quarter. Above a mid speed that surface scales wheel velocity by 99 hundredths per frame when a global flag is set, and above a lower speed it spawns dirt at the wheel. At high speed it also starts a random wheel wobble capped at 14. On surface code 5, above a high speed, wheel velocity scales by 63 sixty-fourths per frame, with a front grip of one half and a rear grip of one quarter. Rear wheels always lose grip first, which makes the tail step out when a car drops a wheel off the track.

constants.name: roughVelocityScale
constants.unit: numerator and denominator in hexadecimal, per frame, rate unverified

constants.name: slickVelocityScale
constants.unit: numerator and denominator in hexadecimal, per frame, rate unverified

cards.name: Gear bands and engine rpm
cards.summary: Each gear covers a speed band, and rpm rises linearly across the band from its low to its high value
cards.behavior: A gear table gives each gear a start speed, an end speed, a low rpm and a high rpm. With the automatic gearbox, the gear is the band that contains the current speed, and rpm interpolates linearly inside it. The top gear runs up to the car maximum speed. After an upshift, automatic selection waits 20 frames. With the manual gearbox the gear stays put: below its band rpm scales down from the low value, and above it rpm holds at the high value. In most game modes, a manual car pushed past its band also gets a forward nudge of 5 speed units. Reverse holds rpm at 10. A manual downshift drops rpm to the new gear low value at once.

constants.name: overBandNudge
constants.unit: speed in 16.16 fixed point, hexadecimal, scale unverified

cards.name: Drive force and coasting
cards.summary: Throttle adds a gear-ratio force each frame, reduced outside the gear band, and lifting off costs a fixed speed per frame
cards.behavior: With throttle held, each frame adds the gear ratio to speed until the target speed. With a manual gearbox, a car below its band gets the ratio scaled by speed plus 80 over the band start. A car above its band gets the ratio scaled by 16 over the excess plus 16. A car inside its band gets a bonus of one sixth. The automatic gearbox only applies the over-band falloff in top gear. An optional assist multiplies a human car force by its rank among the human players, so the trailing player in split screen gets twice the force. The force is then multiplied by seven quarters, and one sixteenth of the draft bonus is added. Without throttle, speed falls by 4 units per frame toward the target. A car out of fuel or with a flagged engine gets no force.

constants.name: inBandBonusDenominator
constants.unit: fraction denominator, per frame, rate unverified

constants.name: finalScaleNumerator
constants.unit: multiplier before subtracting one share and dividing by 4, static

constants.name: draftShareShift
constants.unit: bit shift on draft bonus, divides by 16, static

constants.name: coastLoss
constants.unit: speed in 16.16 fixed point, hexadecimal, scale unverified, per frame, rate unverified

cards.name: Slipstream draft
cards.summary: A car directly behind another inside a range gains a speed bonus that grows as the gap closes
cards.behavior: Draft range comes from a setup value: the value minus 50, times 80. For each car pair, the test first rejects any axis gap larger than that range. It then rotates the gap into the trailing car frame. The leading car must sit ahead, inside the range, and within twice a body extent of the trailing car center line. The bonus is the range minus the forward gap, divided by a strength value of 15000 over the setup value minus 70. One sixteenth of the bonus feeds the drive force each frame, so bump-drafting close behind a leader pays the most.

constants.name: rangeScale
constants.unit: world units per setup step, hexadecimal, static

cards.name: Bump contact speed exchange
cards.summary: Overlapping cars are pushed apart and both speeds are set near their average, one car gaining and the other losing a little
cards.behavior: Contact uses a box from each car model: half-width minus 10 and a length allowance shorter by 30 for two computer cars or by 15 otherwise. When the cars overlap below the crash speed, both are moved apart along the lateral axis of the first car. Their speeds become the mean of the two speeds, plus 10 for one car and minus 10 for the other, picked by the contact direction. Another contact branch adds an impulse, clamped to 50 on each axis, to the wheel velocities. A human car that side-swipes a computer car slows the computer car by 5.

constants.name: bumpSpeedOffset
constants.unit: speed in 16.16 fixed point, hexadecimal, scale unverified

constants.name: sideSwipeSlow
constants.unit: speed in 16.16 fixed point, hexadecimal, scale unverified, negative five

cards.name: Contact crash threshold and sparks
cards.summary: High closing speed turns a contact into a crash state, and medium hits throw sparks with a random extra effect
cards.behavior: The closing speed of a pair is the length of their relative velocity. At 301 or more, the contact sets a crash response and switches each eligible car to the crash routine, so the car spins out of control. Below that, closing speeds of 46 or more spawn a contact effect, and 121 or more add a heavier effect. Each tier also rolls a one-in-ten chance of a second effect. When cars overlap deeply at low speed, both cars are placed 800 units from their midpoint along the line between them, which prevents the cars from stacking inside each other.

constants.name: extraEffectOdds
constants.unit: one in this many, hexadecimal, per contact

cards.name: Wall scrape and rebound
cards.summary: A glancing wall hit scrubs speed by the contact angle, and a firm hit bounces the car off with effects and can wreck it
cards.behavior: Headings use 1024 units per turn. When the car meets the wall at less than 140 units of angle, steering is zeroed and speed drops by twice the angle plus one sixteenth of speed. Each touching corner then gets a rebound impulse of three quarters of the velocity into the wall, applied along the wall normal. Impulses of 51 or more call a contact routine, 101 or more spawn an effect at the car, and 176 or more roll a chance for a second effect that rises with impulse. In one contact branch, a car with speed 371 or more switches to the crash routine.

constants.name: glancingAngle
constants.unit: heading units of 1024 per turn, hexadecimal, static

constants.name: speedShareShift
constants.unit: bit shift, divides speed by 16, per contact

constants.name: wreckSpeed
constants.unit: speed units, 16.16 fixed point integer part, scale unverified, hexadecimal

cards.name: Lap counting and fuel use
cards.summary: A lap counts when a car moves from the last track sections into the first ones, and human cars burn fuel by rpm
cards.behavior: Each car remembers its last track section. A move from section 11 or later into a section below 5 adds a lap. A move from section 0 back into section 11 or later removes one, so a car cannot gain laps by reversing over the line. A car past the lap limit is marked as finished. Every 32 ticks of the race clock each human car burns fuel equal to rpm divided by a fuel rate, and an empty tank stops the drive force. Race progress for the whole field is lap times 1000 plus section. The spotter calls the laps every 5 laps below lap 50 and every 10 laps below lap 100.

constants.name: fuelIntervalMask
constants.unit: race clock mask, every 32 ticks, rate unverified

cards.name: Running order and finish order
cards.summary: Positions sort by lap and section every 20 updates, ties break by distance along the section, and finishers get a lock-in bonus
cards.behavior: Every update the car list is sorted by track section for nearby checks. Every 20 updates, or on demand, each car gets a race key of lap plus one, times 1000, plus section plus a finish bonus. Cars sort by that key. Equal keys break by projecting both cars onto the section heading and comparing forward distance. A car that has passed the lap limit, or any car once a race-end flag is set, gets a permanent bonus of 30 minus its place, times 100000, so finish order cannot change. In time trials the player place comes from comparing the lap time against 23 stored times.

constants.name: lapKeyScale
constants.unit: race key units per lap, static

constants.name: finishScale
constants.unit: race key units per place, static

cards.name: Caution period and restart
cards.summary: A caution hands the player car to the computer driver for a fixed time, then counts down to a green-flag restart
cards.behavior: When a caution starts, the player car switches to the automatic gearbox and is driven by the same routine as the field. Fuel use is suspended, and a timer starts at 600 frames. The caution lasts until the timer runs out and every car has cleared its pending state flags. A car pointing more than 64 heading units off the track direction requests a field realignment step. The restart countdown then runs 100 frames. At 80 the flag display changes, below 50 the player regains control with the original gearbox, and at 40 normal racing resumes.

constants.name: offLineHeading
constants.unit: heading units of 1024 per turn, hexadecimal, static

cards.name: Scripted field crashes
cards.summary: A few cars are picked at the start to wreck later, each after a random countdown, when running near full speed
cards.behavior: At race start, the crash count comes from two race settings, each divided by 50, plus a random term, and is scaled by the field size. Distinct cars are picked at random, and each gets a random countdown that scales with the lap count. Every 200 frames, when no crash is active and no caution is running, each candidate counts down by one. At zero, a computer car crashes once its speed passes nine tenths of a reference speed. A human candidate crashes once it is within 10 speed units of its own maximum. The crash is announced, and smoke spawns at the car center with a random offset of 100 units each way.

constants.name: speedShareNumerator
constants.unit: tenths of a reference speed, static

constants.name: playerMargin
constants.unit: speed in 16.16 fixed point, hexadecimal, scale unverified

cards.name: Opponent passing and traffic avoidance
cards.summary: A computer car looks a few sections ahead, steers to a point beside a slower car, or matches its speed when the lane is blocked
cards.behavior: A pass is possible when the car is faster and the speed difference divided by 20 covers the section gap, which must be below 2. Each frame the car checks others within the speed difference over 50 plus 1 sections, at most 5. It rotates each into its own frame. A car more than 200 units to the side, inside a side window of 400 plus a heading term up to 250, and with a forward offset between four times the closing speed minus 230 and 1350, triggers a lane check. If the lane is closed, the car takes the other speed plus or minus 40. Cars wider than the window are ignored. An overtaking target sits 1600 units ahead of the slower car and 350 units to one side. A car 1001 to 1349 units ahead makes this car match its speed minus 1 when that car is fast, or close the gap by a twentieth of the difference.

constants.name: passGapDivisor
constants.unit: speed difference per section of gap, static

constants.name: lookAheadDivisor
constants.unit: speed units per section of look-ahead, static

constants.name: blockedSpeedOffset
constants.unit: speed in 16.16 fixed point, hexadecimal, scale unverified
